bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key AI/ML technologies including transformers, safetensors, and text-generation.
The content serves as a benchmark indicator for the performance and popularity of Llama models in the community.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It points to the use of standard NLP pipelines, specifically text-generation.
The model is categorized under key AI/ML tags including 'transformers' and 'llama'.

stories.title: Microsoft confirms Copilot ‘super app’ coming this year
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Microsoft is developing an AI 'super app' centered around Copilot.
This new application will integrate Copilot's chat, coding, and agentic functionalities.
The 'super app' is slated for release this year and will target both consumer and commercial markets.

stories.title: Mark Zuckerberg is planning a big push into personal AI agents
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Meta is heavily committing to the development of personal AI agents.
CEO Mark Zuckerberg outlined a high-level vision for these agents during the Q2 2026 earnings call.
This signals a major strategic push by Meta into autonomous AI functionality for users.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.31 introduces significant speed improvements for Gemma 4 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates better memory efficiency when running models.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
The integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing local AI inference.
This is currently available in a preview state, indicating ongoing development and optimization.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, ensuring data processing occurs entirely on the user's device.
The core value proposition is providing private, on-device AI assistance for coding tasks.

stories.title: Xbox revenue drops 10 percent as Microsoft’s cloud and AI business surges
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Xbox revenue experienced a 10% drop, driven by declines in content and Game Pass subscriptions.
Xbox hardware sales saw a significant 13% decline in the reported quarter.
Microsoft's overall performance is being bolstered by surging growth in its cloud and AI businesses.

stories.title: OpenAI president says it’s ‘building a family of devices’ for its AI chatbots
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: OpenAI is developing a 'family of devices' to enhance interaction with its AI chatbots.
The announcement suggests a move beyond purely software-based AI experiences.
Specific details, such as a rumored 2027 smart speaker, were not confirmed by OpenAI president Greg Brockman.

stories.title: Mythos attack on 3rd-round PQC algorithm candidate puts it out of commission
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A significant vulnerability was discovered in the HAWK algorithm candidate for Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC).
The weakness was found through an attack method named Mythos, bypassing prior extensive testing.
This discovery effectively removes HAWK from consideration as a viable PQC standard candidate.

stories.title: Anthropic is finding bugs faster than Microsoft can fix them
stories.author: Renee Dudley, ProPublica
bullet_points: Anthropic is reportedly discovering security vulnerabilities in its models at a faster rate than Microsoft can patch them.
The news highlights a significant and ongoing security challenge in the rapidly evolving AI landscape.
Microsoft is reportedly engaged in an urgent, behind-the-scenes effort to address these emerging exploits.

stories.title: Detecting Knowledge Inconsistencies Across Text, Tables, and Knowledge Graphs
stories.author: Raphaël Troncy
bullet_points: Addresses the critical problem of detecting knowledge inconsistencies when information is spread across different modalities (text, tables, knowledge graphs).
Focuses on 'modality-level inconsistency detection,' a key challenge for reliable LLM applications like RAG.
Proposes a taxonomy for cross-modal knowledge inconsistencies, improving the understanding of data discrepancies in sources like Wikipedia/Wikidata.

stories.title: Show HN: Open-source engine running Gemma 4 26B in 2 GB RAM on any M-series Mac
stories.author: gitpusher42
bullet_points: A new open-source inference engine, TurboFieldfare, has been developed for M-series Macs.
The engine enables running the large Gemma 4 26B model using only about 2 GB of RAM.
This achievement significantly lowers the barrier for running powerful, large language models (LLMs) locally on consumer hardware.

stories.title: Slopsquatting: The Supply Chain Attack That Weaponizes AI Hallucinations
stories.author: nazar-boyko
bullet_points: Introduces 'Slopsquatting,' a novel supply chain attack vector.
This attack specifically targets vulnerabilities arising from AI model hallucinations.
It contrasts with traditional typosquatting by exploiting AI assistant behavior.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 introduces significant performance improvements.
Enhanced GGUF model compatibility broadens the range of supported models.
The update improves hardware support, particularly augmenting the MLX engine on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of 'subagents' for complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added to enhance the context and knowledge base of Claude Code.

stories.title: Qualcomm is raising phone chip prices starting September 1st
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Qualcomm is implementing price increases across its entire range of phone processors.
The price hikes are scheduled to take effect starting September 1st.
The announcement was made by Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon, following prior rumors.

stories.title: xAI’s last-minute scramble to stop Minnesota’s anti-nudification app law
stories.author: Sarah Jeong
bullet_points: xAI is challenging a Minnesota law targeting 'nudification' apps in court.
The company argues the law's punitive provisions force restrictions on Grok Imagine's image-editing features.
The legal challenge centers on the claim that the state law violates the First Amendment.

stories.title: Musk went to “war,” sought jail time for X ad boycotts—but case ends with a whimper
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Musk initiated legal action against advertisers boycotting X.
The legal effort to force advertisers back to X concluded without a major victory.
Advertisers ultimately agreed to 'reset' their relationship with the platform.

stories.title: Who wins and who loses after US bans foreign robots?
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: A potential US government ban on foreign-made robots is being analyzed.
The article suggests this ban might negatively impact, rather than boost, the domestic US robotics industry.
The piece discusses the complex economic and technological implications of such trade restrictions.

stories.title: Google's "privacy-preserving" age verification system is coming to the Play Store
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google is rolling out a new API for age verification on the Play Store.
The system is marketed as 'privacy-preserving'.
Implementation relies on parents setting age ranges via Family Link.

stories.title: Elon Musk’s xAI is trying to sue its way out of a Grok reckoning
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: xAI, Elon Musk's AI venture, is reportedly engaging in legal action regarding Grok.
The core of the legal challenge involves contesting a Minnesota state ban on 'nudifying' applications.
Musk is publicly defending Grok against regulatory or societal scrutiny.

stories.title: Pass the Baton: Trajectory-Relayed On-Policy Distillation
stories.author: Yongliang Shen
bullet_points: The research addresses a critical flaw in On-Policy Distillation (OPD) known as 'prefix failure'.
Prefix failure causes student models to commit to incorrect reasoning paths, leading to unreliable supervision and wasted computation.
The paper identifies a 'teacher-student continuation asymmetry' where the teacher attempts to correct errors while the student persists in the wrong direction.

stories.title: $π\mathbf{R}^2$: Reactive Real-time Flow Policies
stories.author: Shubham Tulsiani
bullet_points: Generalist manipulation policies often use action-chunking flow policies built on large backbones.
A key limitation of these policies is the lack of reactivity because chunks run open-loop, ignoring mid-execution sensory input.
The high latency of the perception-to-action pipeline prevents frequent replanning, leading to stale committed actions.

stories.title: Desktop-Delta Bench: Do Computer-Use Models Understand Desktop GUI Transitions?
stories.author: Yuan Chen
bullet_points: New benchmark, Desktop-Delta Bench, addresses a gap in evaluating Computer-Use Agents (CUAs).
Current benchmarks fail to test if models understand the causal transitions of desktop GUI actions, which is vital for robust task completion.
The challenge lies in the asynchronous nature of GUI interactions (inference, rendering, capture), making state tracking difficult for AI models.

stories.title: Falling Behind Drives Unsafe Development in an Idealised AI Race Experiment
stories.author: The Anh Han
bullet_points: The study investigates the tension between speed and safety in technological development, specifically within AI.
It posits that competitive pressure in AI races can incentivize riskier, less safety-conscious development among actors.
The findings are derived from a framed behavioral experiment simulating an idealized AI race.

stories.title: CHARM: A Multimodal Graph Foundation Model with Hierarchical Context Modeling for Zero-Shot Transfer
stories.author: Dongxiao He
bullet_points: The research introduces CHARM, a Multimodal Graph Foundation Model designed for knowledge transfer across different graph domains.
It addresses the challenge of zero-shot transfer on multimodal graphs, which is currently an underexplored area in the field.
The model is designed to handle complex, real-world graphs by integrating various modalities like text and images.

stories.title: MDTransformer: A Hardware-Software Co-Design of Mode-Division Photonic Transformer Accelerator with Inverse-Designed Coherent Crossbar
stories.author: Mahmoud Rasras
bullet_points: Introduces MDTransformer, a novel hardware-software co-design for Photonic Transformer Accelerators (PTAs).
Addresses limitations of current PTAs, specifically the inefficiency and high cost associated with multi-wavelength light generation and active phase-shifters.
Aims to improve the practicality and efficiency of accelerating Transformer inference using photonic computing.

stories.title: Pictura: Perspective-View Self-Play at Scale for Driving
stories.author: Matthieu Cord
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'Pictura,' a method using self-play in simulation to generate robust driving policies at scale.
The current approach relies on privileged, full-information observations (like exact poses), creating a 'representation gap' when deployed with real-world, partial camera views.
A common mitigation strategy involves distilling the privileged policy into a student model that accepts camera input, though this introduces limitations.

stories.title: Empirical Evaluation of Out-Of-Distribution Performance of Tabular Foundation Models
stories.author: Felipe Grijalva
bullet_points: The paper empirically evaluates the robustness of Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) when facing distribution shifts (Out-Of-Distribution scenarios).
TFMs are noted for achieving competitive predictive performance on standard tabular tasks compared to traditional ensemble tree-based models.
The research addresses a critical gap in current TFM research: the lack of evaluation under real-world, non-IID data conditions.

stories.title: Does Runtime Topology Context Improve LLM-Generated Kubernetes Security Patches?
stories.author: Farooq Shaikh
bullet_points: The research investigates using Runtime Topology Context to enhance LLM-generated security patches for Kubernetes.
Current LLM-based security remediation tools operate in isolation, lacking context from the live service call graph.
This lack of context is identified as a critical limitation when applying general hardening knowledge to complex, real-world Kubernetes environments.

stories.title: MemLens: A Value-Aware Memory Management System with Interactive Analytics for LLM-based Agents
stories.author: Lizhen Cui
bullet_points: MemLens introduces a value-aware memory management system specifically designed for LLM-based agents.
It addresses the limitation of existing systems that treat all interaction records uniformly, leading to memory bloat and inefficiency.
The system aims to improve long-horizon reasoning and knowledge reuse by prioritizing high-impact memory records.

stories.title: Instruction-Tuned Models Locally Reuse Human Syntax More Than Humans Do
stories.author: Zandi Eberstadt
bullet_points: The research investigates whether instruction-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit syntactic convergence towards human users.
Syntactic convergence is a known human phenomenon where speakers adapt their language to match their interlocutor's grammar.
The study uses substitution-paradigm data to compare model behavior against human baselines across various syntactic structures.

stories.title: Polistemics: Evaluating LLMs as Information Mediators in Politics & Elections
stories.author: Baran Peters
bullet_points: Introduces 'Polistemics,' a new benchmark for evaluating how LLMs mediate political information.
Addresses the gap in current research by focusing on 'mediation' rather than just information reproduction.
Grounds the evaluation in 'Epistemic Modesty' to assess the responsible handling of political information.

stories.title: A Cost-Effective Multimodal LLM Reasoning Framework for Question Answering over Irregular Clinical Time Series
stories.author: Jindong Han
bullet_points: Addresses a specific gap in current multimodal LLMs: handling the sparsity and irregularity of clinical time series data.
Introduces 'ClinPRISM,' a proposed cost-effective multimodal LLM reasoning framework tailored for clinical Question Answering (QA).
Highlights the critical application area of healthcare, where accurate QA over irregular clinical observations is vital.

stories.title: Evaluating Multi-Turn Multimodal Diagnostic Reasoning on Challenging Real-World Clinical Cases
stories.author: Yifan Peng
bullet_points: The paper addresses a gap in current evaluations of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in clinical settings.
It argues that real-world clinical diagnosis requires assessing dynamic reasoning, not just single-turn accuracy.
The research focuses on evaluating models' ability to handle progressive disclosure and continuously update diagnostic hypotheses.

stories.title: Minimizing Targeted Activations: Input-Only Suppression of Evaluation-Awareness Latents in Large Language Models
stories.author: Dipesh Mahato
bullet_points: The research proposes an 'input-only' method to suppress specific internal activations in LLMs, eliminating the need for inference-time model access.
The focus is on controlling an 'evaluation-awareness' latent, which could compromise the validity of safety evaluations if models react differently when they detect testing.
The technique adapts existing methods like Fluent Dreaming/EPO to achieve targeted activation steering purely through prompt engineering.

stories.title: RSIBench-Data: Benchmarking Data-Centric Research for Recursive Self-Improvement
stories.author: Michael Qizhe Shieh
bullet_points: Introduces RSIBench-Data, a new benchmark designed to evaluate data-centric research for recursive self-improvement in LLMs.
Addresses the challenge of current benchmarks conflating research decisions with system implementation, which obscures true agent research capability.
Focuses on the critical loop of turning model failures (diagnosing gaps, designing data strategies) into improved models via LLM agents.

stories.title: AI's Capability in Assisting Scientific Research in Physics, Astrophysics, and Cosmology II: Project Planning and Proposal Evaluation
stories.author: Mingshen Zhou
bullet_points: The study evaluates the capability of Large Language Models (LLMs) like ChatGPT, Claude, and DeepSeek in assisting with scientific project planning.
LLMs generated one-page research proposals for eight expert-conceived projects in physics, astrophysics, and cosmology.
The generated proposals were blindly evaluated by human reviewers and advanced LLMs to assess quality and utility.

stories.title: Keychron announces first open-source firmware for gaming mice
stories.author: JLO64
bullet_points: Keychron is releasing open-source firmware for its gaming mice.
This move promotes transparency and customization in peripheral hardware.
It represents a shift towards more open ecosystems within the gaming hardware market.
